title: Dietary Reference Intakes for Sodium and Potassium
authors: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine; Committee to Review the Dietary Reference Intakes for Sodium and Potassium; Oria M, Harrison M, Stallings VA, editors
funder: Contracts between the National Academy of Sciences and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Food and Drug Administration, Health Canada, National Institutes of Health, Public Health Agency of Canada and U.S. Department of Agriculture; also supported in part by the National Academy of Sciences' W.K. Kellogg Foundation Fund and the National Academy of Medicine's Kellogg Health of the Public Fund.
result: Sodium: Adequate Intake 1500 mg/day for adults aged 19 years and older; Chronic Disease Risk Reduction Intake: reduce intakes if above 2300 mg/day; evidence insufficient for an EAR, RDA or UL. Potassium: Adequate Intake 3400 mg/day for men and 2600 mg/day for women aged 19 years and older; evidence insufficient for a potassium CDRR.
